topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe traditional cancer treatment modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cell cycle and DNA repair vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone-dependent signaling, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair-deficient tumors.

topics.label: Small molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the inhibition of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases, the concept of oncogene addiction, and the molecular mechanisms underlying acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design and therapeutic application of engineered monoclonal antibodies and cytotoxic antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the principles of tumor immune surveillance and methods to harness the immune system against cancer using checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Clinical progress, challenges, and future perspectives in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broad historical survival trends, ongoing therapeutic hurdles such as tumor heterogeneity, and future directions in prevention, detection, and combination therapies.
